back: Growing different crops in turn on the same land in a planned, repeated sequence.
Growing the same crop on the same land year after year.
Alternate deep and shallow roots; legumes with heavy feeders; different families; include a ley or fallow; manure the heavy feeder; suit markets and labour.
Land under grass (sometimes with legumes) for a few years, grazed or cut, then ploughed for crops.
Maize (manure) → legume → deep-rooted crop (e.g. sunflower or cotton) → grass ley; each crop moves one field a year.
Fertility, less fertiliser, pest/disease/witchweed control, better structure, less erosion, spread of labour, income and risk.
Planning and records, land divided, low-value courses, varied implements and skills, markets for every crop.
The heavy feeder, such as maize or tobacco.
Same (grass) family: shared pests, diseases and witchweed carry over.
